questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A 22-year-old presented with pain and stiffness in the neck following a blow with a hockey stick. On examination, the right shoulder is drooping. Which of the following muscles is likely to be paralyzed?
questions.explanation:
Drooping of the shoulder is due to paralysis of the trapezius muscle. Trapezius is innervated by the spinal accessory nerve (CN XI).

Its actions include retraction of the scapula, shrugging the shoulder, and overhead abduction together with serratus anterior. Paralysis causes shoulder droop and slight winging, with prominence of the superior angle of the scapula.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following muscles is not involved in the overhead abduction of the arm?
questions.explanation:
Pectoralis major mainly adducts and medially rotates the arm and is not involved in shoulder abduction.

The first 15 degrees of abduction is initiated by supraspinatus; approximately 15-90 degrees is carried mainly by the middle deltoid; beyond 90 degrees, rotation of the shoulder girdle by trapezius and serratus anterior contributes.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A 38-year-old man had recently joined a gym to improve his physical health. He attempted to lift a 30 kg dumbbell but developed sudden pain in his right arm. He came to the casualty with an abnormal bulge over his arm as shown in the image below. Which of the following tendons is most likely to be injured?
questions.explanation:
The image shows the Popeye sign, classically seen with proximal biceps tendon rupture. The bulge becomes prominent on elbow flexion as the unrestrained muscle fibres contract.

Proximal biceps tendon rupture makes up the large majority of biceps tendon ruptures and often has little effect on overall upper-limb function but produces the characteristic deformity.

The source notes common tendon-rupture sites including quadriceps, Achilles, rotator cuff (especially supraspinatus), and biceps.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: What is the function of the muscle marked as A in the image below, at the metacarpophalangeal joint?
questions.explanation:
The muscle marked A is a lumbrical. Lumbricals flex the metacarpophalangeal joints and extend the proximal and distal interphalangeal joints through the dorsal digital expansion.

They originate from flexor digitorum profundus. The lateral two are unipennate and supplied by the median nerve; the medial two are bipennate and supplied by the ulnar nerve.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Power grip of hand is a function of:
questions.explanation:
Power grip is produced by the extrinsic muscles of the hand, especially the long flexors. Extrinsic muscles originate in the forearm and insert into the hand.

Precision grip is primarily a function of intrinsic hand muscles such as adductor pollicis, palmaris brevis, interossei, lumbricals, thenar and hypothenar muscles.

The marked structure is the second lumbrical, which is supplied by the median nerve. The lateral two lumbricals are supplied by the median nerve and the medial two by the ulnar nerve.

Lumbricals flex the metacarpophalangeal joints and extend both interphalangeal joints.
